description: RMSNorm (optionally with residual add) fused with activation quantization of its output: FP8 per-token / per-1x128-group, or MXFP4 per-1x32 with e8m0 scales. aiter add_rmsnorm_quant / fused_rms_fp8_group_quant / rmsnorm + dynamic_mxfp4_quant fusions.

group.doc: elements per scale: hidden for per-token, 128 for fp8 group, 32 for mxfp4

call: Return the quantized output (fp8 tensor, or packed uint8 view for mxfp4), its scales (as float32; decode e8m0 with reference_f64.decode_e8m0) and residual_out, in contract order. Clone in-place operands inside call().

timing.cache: same as rmsnorm: operands are L2-warm in serving; record read-evict as the measured condition.

negative_controls: compute the scale from amax of the un-normalized x: every scale and every quantized value shifts
round-to-zero instead of round-to-nearest-even in the fp8 cast: a biased one-ulp shift on about half the elements, beyond max_violation_fraction
pitfalls: Quantized outputs flip by one code where the fp32 value lands on a rounding boundary, and a different (correct) reduction order moves which elements do: that is why out_q is noise_relative with a 5e-4 violation budget and mxfp4 bytes are exact up to the same budget, not bit-identical.
Never measure packed fp4 bytes with a relative error; compare bytes, or dequantize both and compare values.
The scale is part of the output: a candidate that changes amax/448 to amax/447 passes a dequantized-value check and breaks the consumer GEMM's numerics.
These ops are bandwidth-bound and microsecond-scale in decode: the eager timing includes ~35-45 us of host dispatch; time in the deployment graph mode.
